invariant: The public (anonymous) form REST doors, moved here whole from `rest-server.ts` (#23050 slice 11): `GET {base}/forms/:slug` and `POST {base}/forms/:slug/submit`, mounted once per base, both reading the form through ONE resolution. ADR-0131 — the metadata an anonymous form request reads is the environment's, as every metadata read is: the view list the doors judge (a withdrawal in any body of a view name closing its form) and the object schema the resolve door narrows are both the environment's, never an organization's (its D6). ADR-0056 — the doors bypass `enforceAuth` because their authorization is DERIVED from the form's own declaration (Option A): the submit runs as `publicFormGrant`, scoped to exactly the form's target object, and writes only the fields the form's sections declare, never a server-managed anchor; a form that declares no fields publishes nothing and accepts nothing. ADR-0112 — that refusal answers the standard catalog's generic 400 code, never a minted synonym. A door that reads another layer's metadata, accepts an undeclared key or an anchor, or authorizes by anything but the form's declaration is the drift these records forbid; the bodies' own comments carry each citation. ADR-0159 — since card ② the doors read a form over BOTH types: the candidates are the effective `form` read (authored `form` items and the projection of the three old `view` shapes, resolved over both types so a stored row that replaces its base's body keeps closing the address), judged against the effective lists and the per-package layers of both `form` and `view`, old shapes projected first; narrowing only, in both directions; identity is the served name and the whole item; a stored body the projection cannot read closes the links it names (rule 7). A door that reads one type alone, or lets a slug match decide a withdrawal, can re-open a withdrawn public form.
